1.title: ITIL and AI
1.text: Welcome to Module thirteen: eye til and A I. It covers the exam area eye til and A I. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Define A I, A I maturity, generative A I and agentic A I. Understand how A I assists product and service development, automates processes and is used across the value chain activities. Define A I governance. Understand the eye til A I Capability Model. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: eye til and A I (two point five percent). Exam format: forty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes; twenty-six correct answers (sixty-five percent) pass. Validated against: the official eye til Foundation (Version five) syllabus, version five point zero (February two thousand twenty-six).

1.title: Key AI terms
1.text: Key A I terms. Artificial intelligence (A I). Systems that perform tasks that normally need human intelligence, such as learning, reasoning, understanding language. A I maturity. How capable and well governed an organization is in using A I, from first experiments to everyday use. Generative A I (gen A I). A I that creates new content (text, images, code) from prompts. Agentic A I. A I that acts toward a goal on its own: it plans, decides and takes actions, often using tools, with limited human steps.

1.title: Key AI terms, continued
1.text: Key A I terms. A I governance. The direction and control of how A I is selected, used and monitored so it is responsible, safe and aligned with the organization's goals and rules. Exam tip: gen A I creates content. Agentic A I takes actions. A I governance is governance applied to A I. eye til is not a technical A I framework; it provides structure, collaboration, governance and continual improvement for using A I.

1.title: How AI helps
1.text: How A I helps. Product and service development. Drafting requirements, generating test cases, suggesting designs, reviewing code. Automating processes. Routing and classifying tickets, drafting replies, self-service answers. Across the value chain activities. Discover: analyze feedback; design: prototypes; build: code help and tests; operate: spot anomalies; support: suggest fixes and answers. A I is guided by the guiding principles: for example, focus on value (use A I where it supports real outcomes), start where you are (reuse existing data and models), and optimize and automate (improve first, then automate).

1.title: The ITIL AI Capability Model
1.text: The eye til A I Capability Model. The eye til A I Capability Model groups A I into six capabilities so organizations can see which risks and opportunities each one brings and govern accordingly. Creation. Generating new content or solutions. Curation. Selecting and organizing information and outputs. Clarification. Making things clear: interpreting requests, explaining. Cognition. Analysis and reasoning: patterns, predictions, decisions. Communication. Natural interaction: chat, voice, virtual assistants. Coordination. Orchestrating actions across systems, often autonomously. Exam tip: Only one mark is about A I, so learn the six capability names and the difference between generative (creates content) and agentic (acts toward a goal).

1.title: The ITIL AI Capability Model, continued
1.text: The eye til A I Capability Model. The figure shows this: The six A I capabilities: creation, curation, clarification, cognition, communication, coordination. Exam tip: The six capabilities all start with C. Remember creation, curation, clarification, cognition, communication, coordination. The wording may vary between sources.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A tool writes a first draft of a project plan from a short prompt. Which term fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Generative A I. It creates new content from a prompt.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. An A I assistant plans several steps, calls tools, and updates tickets on its own to reach a goal. Which term fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Agentic A I. Acting toward a goal on its own is agentic A I.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which statements are C O R R E C T? (one) A I governance directs and controls how A I is used. (two) eye til is mainly a technical A I framework. (three) gen A I creates new content. (four) A I cannot support any lifecycle activity. The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: one and three. A I governance directs A I use, and gen A I creates content.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Identify the missing word(s). blank describes how capable and well governed an organization is in using A I. The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A I maturity. That is A I maturity.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which capability in the eye til A I Capability Model covers orchestrating actions across systems? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Coordination. Coordination orchestrates actions.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. How many capabilities does the eye til A I Capability Model describe? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Six. It describes six capabilities.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Define generative A I. Answer: A I that creates new content from prompts. Question two. What is agentic A I? Answer: A I that plans, decides and acts toward a goal with limited human steps. Question three. Define A I governance. Answer: The direction and control of how A I is selected, used and monitored.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Name the six A I capabilities. Answer: Creation, curation, clarification, cognition, communication, coordination. Question five. Name one way A I can support the operate activity. Answer: Spotting anomalies. Question six. What is A I maturity? Answer: How capable and well governed the organization is in using A I.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. gen A I or agentic A I: creates content or acts toward a goal. A I governance: direct and control A I use. A I maturity: capability and governance in using A I. Six capabilities: creation, curation, clarification, cognition, communication, coordination. Value chain: A I can help every lifecycle activity.
